title: diggs-diff 1.0
description: The difference between two DIGGS files at model level, as pydiggs.diff.compare() writes it (pyDIGGS 1.13 and later). Open for consumers: objects accept unknown fields, so a 1.0 consumer accepts any 1.x document. A new optional field is a minor version; anything else is a new major. Nothing is converted: a change of unit is a change.

$schema.description: URL of the schema the document follows.

schema_version.description: Major.minor of diggs-diff; a pre-release adds -beta.N (1.0-beta.1 was written by pyDIGGS 1.12).

identical.description: True only when nothing differs and the comparison finished (complete). A number written differently (reformatted) and a record's own gml:id (renamed) are not differences.

complete.description: False when a limit stopped the comparison, a file was read in part, or values were not there to compare; see limits_hit and notes. An incomplete comparison is never identical.

limits_hit.description: What stopped the comparison or what it could not look at; empty exactly when complete. max_changes: the list of changes was cut. time_budget: the time ran out. old_read_incomplete, new_read_incomplete: that file was read in part. old_results_not_read, new_results_not_read: that side is a model read without the values of its result tables, so their cells were not compared. A later minor version may add a value.

summary.description: Node counts per collection (features, samples, measurements, layers, components ...). Exact when only max_changes stopped the list; partial after a time_budget stop.

value_changes.description: How many values differ (every listed value change counts, listed or not).

reformatted.description: How many values are written differently but are equal: a number (1.50 and 1.5), the separators of a result set whose values read the same, a declared type written another way (double and float).

renamed.description: How many records were matched by their natural key and have a different gml:id in the two files. Not a difference: such a record counts as unchanged unless a value of it differs.

changes.description: Ordered by collection, then key, then path. At most max_changes entries (changes plus value changes). A record with op reformatted or renamed did not change; it is listed only on request.

notes.description: Findings of step diff: diff.ambiguous-match, diff.limit, diff.timeout.

allOf.description: Identical means complete, and nothing counted or listed as a difference.
A complete comparison names no limit; an incomplete one names at least one.

note.description: A finding of step diff, as diggs-findings 1.2 writes one. Open, like every object in this schema: a field a later findings minor adds leaves a 1.0 document valid.

rule_id.description: Stable id; the part before the first dot equals step.

op.description: reformatted: the same value written differently (1.50 and 1.5; the separators of a result set whose values read the same; double and float). renamed: the record's own gml:id differs (a value with path gml_id), or, on a record, its id differs and no value changed. Neither is a difference.

collection.description: Where the record lives: document, projects, features, samples, measurements, layers, components ... What a file holds outside every record (the attributes of its root element, the text between its members) is the document's: compared with its record, or listed as the root element (element Diggs) when the two files have no pair of document records.

truncated.description: True when name or a key was cut to 200 characters.

path.description: Which value: name, params.<element>, interval.top, results[0].columns[<key>].cells[@<index>] ...; gml_id is the record's own gml:id; a path that starts with xml. is content of the file that the model does not keep, below the record (xml.Diggs[1] is the root element). A path that would be longer than 1,000 characters keeps its first 200 and its last 400, around a digest of the whole path, so two different paths stay different.

old.description: The value in the old file as JSON (a quantity is its text and unit, e.g. "1.50 ft"); null when the old file has none. Text is cut to 200 characters and lists to 200 items.

new.description: The value in the new file; null when the new file has none.

at.description: XPath of the record in the new file. An XPath that would be longer than 1,000 characters is shortened as a path is, and is then no longer an XPath.

truncated.description: True when old or new was cut.
